question: Should the browser SSRF boundary cover every navigation-capable Playwright interaction before this PR merges, or should maintainers intentionally accept only hover, drag, and scroll as the bounded repair?
rationale: The new request-stage mechanism is materially stronger than the existing sibling post-action checks, and choosing a permanently split enforcement boundary is a security-owner decision rather than a routine implementation detail.

options.title: Complete sibling coverage
options.body: Extend the page-scoped request guard to click, submit/type, press, coordinate click, select, fill, and evaluation paths that can navigate, with focused and live proof.

options.title: Accept bounded repair
options.body: Land the three-action protection only after explicitly documenting and separately tracking the remaining request-stage gaps.

recommendation.title: Complete sibling coverage
recommendation.body: Extend the page-scoped request guard to click, submit/type, press, coordinate click, select, fill, and evaluation paths that can navigate, with focused and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged history shows direct work on delayed browser navigation blocks and the central browser ownership boundary, while this PR’s discussion defines the intended bounded claim.
